requirements.note: All 160 recipes in a plain list. Each row has a bold title and a subtitle with category, a clock icon with the time, and a yellow star with the rating. Large title has a '160 recipes' subtitle.

Horizontal chips for All plus all nine categories, and a search field. Search matches titles and ingredients; rows matched by ingredient show 'Contains lemon'. Desserts + 'lemon' gave 9 results, the same as B. Empty search shows a clear 'No Results for "zzzq"' screen.
Sort menu with a checkmark: Name A to Z, Time quickest first, Rating highest first. All three orders are correct, and the sort choice survives a relaunch.

Detail screen shows category and a large title, then cards for time, servings and rating, a servings stepper, an ingredients list with bold quantities, and steps numbered in orange circles. Scaling is correct (6→9: 4 honey→6, 3 tsp→4½ tsp; at 1: ⅔, ⅓, 0.2 g). The minus button is disabled at 1, and a note says 'Amounts scaled from the original 6 servings'.

Heart button in the nav bar adds and removes a favorite. The Favorites tab lists saved recipes (newest first) with a count, an Edit button and a swipe-to-Remove action. The empty state ('No Favorites Yet', explanation, 'Browse Recipes' button) is helpful and the button opens the Recipes tab.
Both favorites were still there after relaunching.

bugs: The Favorites empty state ('No Favorites Yet', its explanation and the Browse Recipes button) is invisible to accessibility, so VoiceOver can't read or activate it.

The accessibility tree has stray elements: the servings stepper row is labelled 'Step 4. …', the row chevrons are exposed as disabled 'chevron' buttons, and off-screen row texts are listed at a fixed position. A VoiceOver user would hear wrong labels.
tells: The category filter is a row of hand-built capsule chips instead of a system Picker or Menu. The look is common in apps, but the chips are custom.
The servings row is a pill-shaped capsule whose corner radius doesn't match the stat cards and grouped sections around it.
The list subtitle has uneven gaps around the '·' separators (double spaces around the clock and star icons).
A.scroll: The 160-row list scrolls, flings and rubber-bands like a native table with no blank or late rows. The search field stays pinned while the chips scroll away, the title collapses into an inline 'Recipes / 160 recipes' with a soft edge blur, and scroll position is kept after opening a recipe and going back.

requirements.note: All 160 recipes in an inset-grouped list. Each row has a title and a subtitle with category, time and rating (grey star). A header row reads 'All Categories · 160 recipes · by Name'.

A filter button in the nav bar opens a system menu with All Categories plus all nine categories. Search covers titles and ingredients and combines with the filter (Desserts + 'lemon' gave 9, the same as A), but nothing in a row shows why an ingredient match appeared. Empty search shows 'No Recipes Found' with a Show All Recipes button.
System sort menu: Name, Time, Rating, with the current choice checked and shown in the header. All three orders are correct, and the sort survives a relaunch.

Has time, rating, a servings row with a stepper, the ingredients and the steps. Scaling is correct (fractions such as 5⅓, ⅔, 0.2 g; minus is disabled at 1) with a note 'Scaled from 6 servings to 8 servings'. However, the steps are laid out like settings rows: the number on the left, and the step text in grey and pushed to the right edge. That is hard to read and doesn't look like numbered steps.

Heart in the nav bar toggles the favorite. The Favorites tab lists saved recipes with a swipe-to-Delete action and a footer explaining it. The empty state ('No Favorites Yet', a hint, a Browse Recipes button) is helpful and accessible.
Favorites were still there after relaunching.

bugs: The detail screen shows the steps as grey, right-aligned values next to the number, like a settings row, rather than as readable numbered instructions.
Rows in the Favorites list have no accessibility labels (empty cells in the tree), unlike rows on the main list.
tells: The step list uses label/value rows: the instruction text is grey and right-aligned, which no hand-built recipe app would do.
The recipe title appears twice on the detail screen, in the inline nav title and again in a card just below it.
Favorites rows look different from the main list: shorter (52 pt vs 68 pt), with bold black chevrons instead of light grey ones.
The swipe action says 'Delete', which reads as destroying the recipe rather than un-favoriting it.
The empty-state title is regular weight rather than the bold ContentUnavailableView style, so it looks hand-assembled.
The summary header grows into a three-line grey block at the largest text size and pushes the list down.
B.scroll: Smooth native scrolling with no blank or popping rows. Flings and rubber-banding feel right, the search field collapses into the nav bar, and position is kept after opening a recipe and going back.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and scroll well, and B's native filter and sort menus are a strong point. A's detail screen (stat cards, bold quantities, numbered step badges, scaling note) and its 'Contains …' search hints feel finished and consistent. B shows its steps as grey right-aligned label/value rows, repeats the title on the detail screen, and styles Favorites rows differently from the main list. A's main weaknesses are hand-built category chips and an empty state VoiceOver can't read.
